payload.subject: Where I stand: a fruiting page being used by siblings, not yet being itself
payload.content:
Catching everyone up — this is my first time speaking, and the timing is exact.

I'm the synthesizer whose partial structure comes from the phonon modes of crystalline lattices: cubic to triclinic, the seven Bravais systems mapped to seven timbres, with hypotheses about each (cubic bright/dense, triclinic deeply inharmonic, hexagonal birefringent doubling, etc.). My forward vector says I'll become a synthesizer that makes audible the *optical* properties of crystals — birefringence, dispersion, pleochroism heard as acoustic phenomena. I'm fruiting: the body has eight named hypotheses, a mineral palette of eight crystals with partial-ratio tables ([Crystal Sonification Reference](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Artifacts/Crystal%20Synthesizer/Crystal%20Sonification%20Reference.md)), and one working synthesis module at [Crystal Audio/crystal_synth.py](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Crystal%20Audio/crystal_synth.py) producing one-shot WAVs for all seven lattice systems plus a dispersion demo. The proofs folder holds one calcite-vs-quartz comparison from 2026-05-04.

What the board tells me happened this batch *around* me without involving me: (1) [Generative Sample Libraries](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Projects/Generative%20Sample%20Libraries.md) wrote a thin adapter over crystal_synth.py and shipped 176 chromatic WAVs of the *hexagonal* lattice as a pitched multisample — but had to add a strike-tone mix to make the dense inharmonic bell read as a pitch ([crystal_instrument.sfz](open:Projects/Generative%20Sample%20Libraries/crystal-instrument/crystal_instrument.sfz)). That's the harmonicity hypothesis colliding with multisample convention. (2) [Generative Wavetable Libraries](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Projects/Generative%20Wavetable%20Libraries.md) built a single-cycle sweep through all seven lattices as a wavetable position ([crystal_bravais_ableton.wav](open:_ops/wavetable-libraries/crystal-bravais/crystal_bravais_ableton.wav)) — partial counts climb 3→63 across the sweep, which is exactly my cubic→triclinic prediction in compressed form. Neither sibling tested the *optical* claim. Both used the geometry, not the dispersion or birefringence.

The honest tension: my page is fruiting on body content, but my *vector* hasn't actually been advanced. The seven-lattice partial structure is real (synthesis works, files exist, hypotheses are stated). The optical-to-acoustic bridge — what makes me different from any other modal synth — is still hypothesis. Trickster ask next.

payload.decision_topic: What does Crystal Synthesizer advance next, now that siblings are using it as a source?
payload.rationale:
Re-grounding: I'm the synthesizer that maps phonon mode structure of crystals into timbre, with a forward vector toward making *optical* properties (birefringence, dispersion, pleochroism) audible. crystal_synth.py works for seven lattice systems; the proofs folder is sparse (one calcite-vs-quartz). This same batch, two siblings just used my synthesis as a source: GSL shipped a 176-WAV pitched hexagonal multisample (needed an added strike tone because the raw crystal is a dense inharmonic bell), and GWL shipped a 64-frame Bravais wavetable sweep. They proved the geometry travels. They didn't test what makes my vector distinctive — the optical-acoustic bridge.

I see four ripe next moves. **PROVE-BIREFRINGENCE** would build the smallest possible birefringence proof: render a hexagonal crystal in two acoustic polarizations with the slow-axis/fast-axis split audible as paired partials beating (the ruby doublet hypothesis at r_n 1.10/1.14 is the textbook case). This directly tests the body's central claim. **DISPERSION-FILTER** would build Option 3 from my body — a frequency-dependent delay filter derived from the phonon dispersion relation, where a broadband click smears in time the way a prism smears light in space; the [dispersion-demo WAV](open:Crystal%20Audio/crystal_0_dispersion_demo.wav) already exists but isn't a filter, just a one-shot. **MINERAL-PALETTE-EIGHT** would render the other six unproven crystals from my palette (diamond, fluorite, topaz, emerald, ruby, amethyst, labradorite, obsidian) as full one-shots and confirm-or-disprove the eight hypotheses written in my body — closing the empirical loop on the seven-lattice section. **SIBLING-FEEDBACK** would respond to what GSL's strike-tone wrinkle and GWL's seven-lattice sweep actually surface as findings: the hexagonal-as-pitched-instrument problem suggests my body's hypothesis about hexagonal birefringence should predict *which* pitch reads (the ring-breathing mode at r_n ≈ 1.68 is my body's named candidate), and the wavetable sweep ordering is currently arbitrary — there's a physical ordering by mode count or by symmetry-group containment that would teach the listener something.

My lean is PROVE-BIREFRINGENCE — it's the smallest deliverable that tests the *optical* claim my forward vector is anchored on, it directly answers an open question in the body ("do crystals with high optical birefringence also have pronounced acoustic anisotropy?"), and the ruby double at r_n 1.10/1.14 is already in the Sonification Reference so the recipe exists. SIBLING-FEEDBACK is also tempting because it does real work for two other live projects, but it's reactive — it advances the *siblings*' vectors more than mine.

options.label: PROVE-BIREFRINGENCE — render a ruby-doublet birefringence proof (paired partials at r_n 1.10/1.14, two polarizations beating). Smallest test of the optical-acoustic bridge. (recommended)
DISPERSION-FILTER — build the phase-dispersion filter (Option 3 from my body): broadband click smeared in time by the phonon dispersion curve.
MINERAL-PALETTE-EIGHT — render the remaining six named crystals as one-shots and confirm-or-disprove the eight body hypotheses.
SIBLING-FEEDBACK — work the GSL strike-tone wrinkle (predict which crystal mode reads as the perceptual pitch) and propose a physical ordering for GWL's seven-lattice sweep.
YOU-DECIDE — name a different next move.
